annotations.title: Virgins.
annotations.text: Theſe virgins fiue wiſe, and fiue fooliſh, ſignifie that in the Church militant there be good and bad: which bad ſhal be ſhut out at the later day, although they haue lampes (that is faith) as the other, ◦ becauſe their lampes are out, that is, their faith is dead without charity and good workes to lighten them Greg. ho. 12.

annotations.title: Lampes.
annotations.text: Theſe lampes lighted, be good workes, namely of mercy, and the laudable conuerſation which ſhineth before men. Aug. ep. 120, c. 33.

annotations.title: Oyle.
annotations.text: ◦ This oyle is the right inward intention directing our workes to Gods glorie, and not to the praiſe of our ſelues in the ſight of men. Aug. ep. 120, c. 33.

annotations.title: With vſurie.
annotations.text: Vſurie is here taken for the lawful gaine that a man getteth by wel employing his goods. When God geueth vs any talent or talents, he looketh for vſurie, that is, for ſpiritual increaſe of the ſame by our diligence and induſtrie.

annotations.title: That which he ſeemeth to haue.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> He is ſaid to haue Gods gifts, that vſeth them, and to ſuch an one God wil increaſe his giftes. He that vſeth them not, ſeemeth to haue, rather then hath them. and from him God wil withdraw that which before he gaue.

annotations.title: Separate.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> Lo here is the ſeparation, for in the Church militant they liued both together. As for Heretikes, they went out of the Church before, and ſeparated them ſelues, and therfore are not to be ſeparated here, as being iudged already.

notes.text: Good and bad in the Church.

annotations.title: Come ye, 41 get ye away.
annotations.text: ◦ It is no incongruity that God ſhould ſay, Goe into euerlaſting fire, to them that by their free wil haue repelled his mercie: and to the other, Come ye bleſſed of my father, take the kingdom prepared for them, that by their free wil haue receiued faith, and confeſſed their ſinnes and done penance. Aug. li. 2 act. cum Fel. Manich. c. 8.

notes.text: Heauen is the reward of good workes, and Hel of the contrarie.

annotations.title: You gaue me.
annotations.text: Hereby we ſee how much almes-deedes and al workes of mercy preuaile towardes life euerlaſting, and to blot out former ſinnes. Aug. in Ps. 49.

annotations.title: Gaue me not.
annotations.text: He chargeth them not here that they beleeued not, but that they did not good workes. For ſuch did beleeue, but they cared not for good workes, as though by dead faith they might haue come to heauen. Aug. de fid. & op. c. 15. & ad Dulcit. q. 2. to. 4.
